help.intro: Reviews are written by buyers on the storefront - nothing here creates one. This screen is the moderation queue: what to publish, what to take down, and what the score beside a product is made of.
help.step_1_body: Unlike a comment, no review is published unread, whoever wrote it. A review is a lasting claim about something being sold and it is averaged into the product's score, so the one thing that could not be undone afterwards - publishing it - is not done first.
help.step_2_title: Read what the score is made of
help.step_2_body: A buyer scores any of quality, price, service and delivery, and at least one of them. The average is over the ones they gave, never over the four that exist, so a review scored on two is not penalized against one scored on four. The list shows that average; the detail window shows each score behind it.
help.step_3_body: A review can name the variant it is about - the 32 cm, the black M - or none at all when it was written from the product page. Filtering by variant returns only the reviews that name it, which is what the storefront shows beside that variant.
help.step_4_body: The status window offers only the moves allowed from where the review is now, and nothing returns it to pending. Approving is what publishes it - and also what lets readers comment on, rate or report it, since all three are refused against a review that is not approved.
help.step_5_body: Update changes the text, the pin and the verified-buyer badge. The scores are the buyer's and are not editable here at all. Nothing sets the badge on its own: it is a claim the dashboard stands behind, so it is checked by hand once the purchase has been confirmed.
help.step_6_title: Find your way through the queue
help.step_6_body: Filter by status for the queue itself, or by product, variant, author, rating floor, pin and badge. Search matches the review text. Deleting is soft, so 'Show deleted' is what a restore reaches a row through.
help.note: Deleting a review frees the slot: one live review per buyer per product, so the author may write a new one straight away - and restoring the old one then answers 409, because the slot is taken. There is one review per buyer per product however many variants they bought.
